objectives: I can understand a short diary entry by reading and listening.
I can ask and answer questions about what someone did yesterday.
I can write 4 sentences about my own yesterday using the Simple Past.

stages.name: Opening — retrieval and bridge
stages.purpose: Activate prior knowledge of past forms and give pupils a clear picture of what the lesson will ask them to do.

procedure.text: Quick fire (whole class, oral): call out base verbs one at a time — go, have, do, eat. Pupils call back the Simple Past form. Accept any correct attempt.
Think-write: 'Write 2 things you did last weekend. Use English.' Pupils write independently in exercise books.
Partner swap: pupils check each other's verb forms. Teacher circulates, notes the most common error for Stage 2.
Bridge (spoken): 'You already know some past forms. Today we put them to work — you will listen, read, speak, and write about a full day in the past.'
Write the three 'I can...' objectives on the board. Read aloud, pupils read back quietly.

stages.name: Grammar input — Simple Past
stages.purpose: Introduce the Simple Past rule for regular and key irregular verbs, with explicit contrast against German Perfekt to head off the most common transfer error.

procedure.text: Display the grammar explanation. Read through with class: regular rule (-ed), then six irregular forms (go/went, have/had, do/did, eat/ate, see/saw, be/was-were).

Point to the German Perfekt contrast: 'In German: Ich habe gegessen — two words. In English: I ate — one word, no have.' Model two sentences from the diary: 'Mia woke up at seven.' and 'She ate toast.'
Pupils write one sentence of their own using any irregular form from the list.

stages.name: Reading and listening input
stages.purpose: Give pupils a model of Simple Past in context and build understanding at the 'understand' depth for Reading 2 and Listening 3.

procedure.text: Pupils open the diary entry and read silently.
Teacher reads the diary aloud at natural pace — pupils follow along (listening run).
Comprehension check — ask 4 questions orally: 1. What time did Mia wake up? 2. What did she eat for breakfast? 3. How did she get to school? 4. What did Mia do after school?
Confirm answers with class. Write correct Simple Past forms on the board as they appear in answers.

stages.name: Controlled practice — gap-fill
stages.purpose: Consolidate recognition and reproduction of key irregular Simple Past forms in a supported (Band 1) format before moving to production.

procedure.text: Display gap-fill exercise. Read instruction aloud: 'Fill each gap with the correct Simple Past form. Use the word bank.' Do first item together as a model.
Pupils complete items 2–6 independently.
Partner check: pupils swap and mark. Teacher reveals answers. Any item more than half the class got wrong: write form on board and briefly revisit rule.

stages.name: Production — speaking then writing
stages.purpose: Move pupils from recognition to genuine production — first oral (Speaking 3), then written (Writing 2) — using sentence frames faded after the first round.

procedure.text: Write speaking frames on board: 'What did you do yesterday at...?' / 'I woke up at...' / 'Then I...' / 'After that I...' / 'Finally I...'. Model one exchange with a volunteer.
Round 1 (frames visible): Partner A asks 'What did you do yesterday?' Partner B answers using at least 3 frames. Then swap. Both partners speak.
Erase all frames from board. 'Now try without the frames — you remember the structure.'
Pupils write 4 sentences about their own yesterday independently. Frames stay erased.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Return to learning intentions for self-assessment and collect written sentences as a formative check.

procedure.text: Point to 'I can...' statements. Pupils rate: thumbs up (confident), sideways (mostly), down (need more). Note rough split.
Pupils hand in books open at written sentences, or teacher photographs pages. Not graded — formative only.
Preview: 'Next lesson — word order with time expressions and more speaking.' Early finishers: open the error-correction worksheet.

differentiationNotes: Weaker: keep speaking frames visible during writing, 3 sentences OK. Stronger: 5th sentence with conjunction (and/but/because), attempt error-correction worksheet in wrap-up.
exercisePlan: Band 1 — gap_fill: 6 daily-routine sentences, key irregular Simple Past forms, full word bank [fk.g.simple_past, fk.k.lesen.2]
Band 2 — reorder: 5 scrambled sentences with time words (yesterday/after/then/finally), no model [fk.g.simple_past, fk.k.schreiben.2]
Band 3 — error_correction: 4 sentences with German-transfer errors (Perfekt for past story, V2 word order, regularised irregular), no error-type hints [fk.g.simple_past]
